title: Understanding Pulsar Magnetospheres with the SKAO
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Oswald01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes. N.B. a version of this article was previously published as part of a Special Issue, linked at arxiv:2512.16157
summary: The SKA telescopes will bring unparalleled sensitivity across a broad radio band, a wide field of view across the Southern sky, and the capacity for sub-arraying, all of which make them the ideal instruments for studying the pulsar magnetosphere. This chapter describes the advances that have been made in pulsar magnetosphere physics over the last decade, and details how these have been made possible through the advances of modern radio telescopes, particularly SKA precursors and pathfinders. It explains how the SKA telescopes would transform the field of pulsar magnetosphere physics through a combination of large-scale monitoring surveys and in-depth follow-up observations of unique sources and new discoveries. Finally, it describes how the specific observing opportunities available with the AA* and AA4 configurations will achieve the advances necessary to solve the problem of pulsar radio emission physics in the coming years.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses how SKA telescopes, with their sensitivity, wide field of view, and sub-arraying capabilities, will advance pulsar magnetosphere physics through monitoring surveys and follow-up observations, particularly using AA* and AA4 configurations to solve pulsar radio emission physics.
AI.motivation: To leverage SKA telescopes' unparalleled sensitivity, broad radio band, wide field of view, and sub-arraying capacity to advance understanding of pulsar magnetosphere physics and solve the problem of pulsar radio emission.
AI.method: Combining large-scale monitoring surveys with in-depth follow-up observations of unique sources and new discoveries, using specific SKA configurations (AA* and AA4).
AI.result: Advances made over the last decade via SKA precursors and pathfinders demonstrate progress; SKA telescopes are expected to transform the field.
AI.conclusion: The specific observing opportunities with AA* and AA4 configurations will achieve the advances necessary to solve pulsar radio emission physics in the coming years.

title: Formation of rotating supergiants via stellar mergers in dense clusters: Implications for black hole natal spins
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Submitted to MNRAS. Comments welcome!
summary: We investigate how massive stellar mergers in young star clusters imprint on black hole spin distributions and the broader implications for gravitational wave sources. The central hypothesis is that angular momentum transferred during stellar mergers substantially affects the spins of the merger products and resulting black holes, with some merger products evolving into collapsar-like objects that retain thick accretion disks that enable efficient spin up. This is in contrast to the more general expectation that black holes form with very small spins, having shed most of their envelope angular momentum via winds and expansion before core collapse. Using roughly 150 N-body models generated with the $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ code, $\texttt{CMC}$, we analyze stellar mergers that lead to black hole formation, prioritizing ``significant'' events with mass ratio $q>0.1$. After identifying optimal candidates from our $\texttt{CMC}$ models, we explore detailed stellar structure and post-merger evolution implications with MESA stellar evolution models to capture angular momentum injection and pre-collapse profiles most relevant for the BH natal spin. In our current dataset representative of Milky Way-like globular clusters, up to roughly half of black holes are formed from such mergers, including up to roughly $10\%$ from significant mergers with $q>0.1$. Preliminary angular momentum estimates indicate substantial spin-up during the merger, and trends with mass ratio and stellar properties suggest strong correlations with the final black hole spin. In some cases, dimensionless spin parameters of $a\simeq 0.5$ or more are expected. This process has important implications for the dynamical formation and retention of gravitational wave sources in clusters.

AI.tldr: Massive stellar mergers in young star clusters can significantly spin up black holes (up to a~0.5) via angular momentum transfer, with up to ~50% of BHs in Milky Way-like globular clusters formed from mergers, impacting gravitational wave source formation.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether angular momentum transferred during stellar mergers can substantially affect black hole spins, challenging the expectation that BHs form with very small spins due to envelope angular momentum loss via winds and expansion.
AI.method: Used ~150 N-body models with Cluster Monte Carlo (CMC) code to analyze stellar mergers leading to BH formation, prioritized significant mergers (q>0.1), then explored detailed post-merger evolution with MESA stellar evolution models to capture angular momentum injection and pre-collapse profiles.
AI.result: Up to ~50% of BHs in Milky Way-like globular clusters form from mergers, ~10% from significant mergers (q>0.1). Preliminary angular momentum estimates show substantial spin-up, with dimensionless spin parameters a~0.5 or more expected in some cases, and strong correlations with mass ratio and stellar properties.
AI.conclusion: Massive stellar mergers provide a mechanism for BH spin-up in clusters, with important implications for dynamical formation and retention of gravitational wave sources.

title: Radio and X-ray Observations of the Transitional Supernova 2019yvr: Insights into the Progenitor Mass-Loss History
comment: 19 pages,9 Figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: The final life stages of the massive star progenitors of stripped-envelope supernovae (SESNe) are still an open question, especially when it comes to the timing and magnitude of the progenitor stripping. Observing SESNe across the electromagnetic spectrum allows for the most direct constraints on mass loss in the final stages of progenitor evolution. In this work, we present radio (GMRT+VLA) and X-ray (Swift+Chandra) observations of SN 2019yvr obtained from 18-1784 days post-explosion. SN 2019yvr was a type Ib supernova (SN Ib, with strong helium but no or little optical hydrogen features) that transitioned into a type IIn supernova (SN IIn, with shock-driven hydrogen features) at $\sim$ 100 days post-explosion. The radio evolution is best-fit by a synchrotron self-absorbed model with a $ρ\propto r^{-1.65 \pm 0.25}$ CSM density profile, suggesting a decreasing mass-loss rate from the progenitor in the years leading up to the explosion. The radio-derived shock speed is high, more than 30,000 km/s at early times, suggesting a compact progenitor star. The combined radio and X-ray data probe CSM that extends from less than $10^{16}$ cm up to $\sim$ 20$\times10^{16}$ cm and was created by mass-loss from $\sim 1-3 \times10^{-5} \rm{M_{\odot} yr^{-1}} $ (assuming a CSM speed of 100 km/s). The combined dataset rules out any dramatic jump in CSM density (which was seen in the optical analog SN 2014C) associated with the emergence of optical hydrogen emission in SN 2019yvr. We place SN 2019yvr in context with similar transitional SNe and discuss implications for the progenitor.

AI.tldr: Radio and X-ray observations of SN 2019yvr (a type Ib supernova that transitioned to type IIn) reveal a decreasing mass-loss rate from its progenitor in the years before explosion, a compact progenitor with shock speeds >30,000 km/s, and rule out a dramatic CSM density jump like that seen in the analog SN 2014C.
AI.motivation: To constrain the final life stages and mass-loss history of stripped-envelope supernova progenitors, particularly regarding the timing and magnitude of progenitor stripping, by observing SESNe across the electromagnetic spectrum.
AI.method: Radio (GMRT+VLA) and X-ray (Swift+Chandra) observations of SN 2019yvr from 18-1784 days post-explosion, modeled with a synchrotron self-absorbed framework to infer the CSM density profile and shock dynamics.
AI.result: The CSM density profile follows ρ ∝ r^{-1.65±0.25}, indicating a decreasing mass-loss rate (~1-3×10^{-5} M⊙/yr) before explosion. Shock speeds exceed 30,000 km/s at early times, implying a compact progenitor. No dramatic CSM density jump is associated with the optical hydrogen emission transition, unlike SN 2014C.
AI.conclusion: SN 2019yvr's progenitor experienced declining mass loss leading up to explosion, was compact, and the transition to SN IIn features was not driven by a sudden CSM density enhancement. The results provide constraints on the final evolution of massive stars that produce stripped-envelope supernovae.

title: Radiation-hydrodynamics of star-disc collisions: From system parameters to outflows and lightcurves
comment: Submitted to A&A, comments are welcome!
summary: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) are nuclear transients producing bright, repeating soft X-ray flares superimposed on quiescent emission. A promising interpretation is that they are powered by star-disc collisions, in which a star crosses an accretion disc around a supermassive black hole, drives shocks, and launches dense outflows from which radiation emerges. We present a systematic study of star-disc collisions, linking the physical parameters of the collision to the resulting outflows and emerging bolometric luminosities. We perform three-dimensional local radiation-hydrodynamics simulations, varying the disc surface density and vertical density profile, stellar velocity and radius, and local collision angle. We focus on the regime where the star remains unperturbed by the collision. We find that the variations of stellar velocity and disc surface density leave the bow shock and outflow morphology largely unchanged. However, faster stars produce brighter flares, while denser discs mainly increase the flare duration. Increasing the stellar radius increases the momentum of the forward outflow and produces brighter and longer flares. More centrally concentrated discs yield brighter and shorter flares because radiation escapes more efficiently through outer low-density layers. More oblique crossings reduce the momentum and luminosity asymmetry of two outflows and lengthen the flares. We provide empirical scalings of the peak luminosity and flare duration with the individual system parameters and apply them to GSN 069. The best candidate solutions favour a star with a radius $\sim R_\odot$ on a retrograde orbit, colliding with a dense post-TDE disc with a vertically concentrated density profile. Our findings suggest that specific combinations of system parameters can reproduce characteristic flare amplitudes, durations, duty cycles, and strong-weak flare patterns observed in QPE sources.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically studies star-disc collisions as the mechanism behind quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) using 3D radiation-hydrodynamics simulations, finding that flare properties depend on stellar velocity, disc density, stellar radius, vertical density profile, and collision angle. Applied to GSN 069, the best fit favors a Sun-like star on a retrograde orbit colliding with a dense, vertically concentrated post-TDE disc.
AI.motivation: To systematically link the physical parameters of star-disc collisions to the resulting outflows and bolometric luminosities, providing a theoretical framework to explain observed QPE properties.
AI.method: Three-dimensional local radiation-hydrodynamics simulations varying disc surface density, vertical density profile, stellar velocity, stellar radius, and collision angle, focusing on the regime where the star remains unperturbed.
AI.result: Faster stars produce brighter flares; denser discs increase flare duration; larger stellar radii yield brighter, longer flares; more centrally concentrated discs give brighter, shorter flares; oblique crossings reduce outflow asymmetry and lengthen flares. Empirical scalings derived and applied to GSN 069, favoring a Sun-like star on a retrograde orbit with a dense, vertically concentrated post-TDE disc.
AI.conclusion: Specific combinations of system parameters can reproduce characteristic flare amplitudes, durations, duty cycles, and strong-weak flare patterns observed in QPE sources, supporting the star-disc collision model.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for the Ly$α$ Forest: CNN-Based Absorber Detection and Characterization
comment: Submitted to MNRAS. (Comments are welcome)
summary: The Ly$α$ forest is a powerful probe of the intergalactic medium and small-scale matter distribution, but deriving absorber properties traditionally requires computationally expensive Voigt-profile fitting. We present a convolutional neural network (CNN) that identifies and characterizes H I Ly$α$ absorbers directly from quasar spectra. The model is trained on synthetic spectra generated from the IllustrisTNG simulation and fitted with the VIPER Voigt-profile fitting code to provide training labels. The network simultaneously predicts absorber presence, column density ($N_{\rm HI}$), Doppler parameter ($b_{\rm HI}$), and line centroid. On simulated spectra, the CNN achieves an F1 score of $\sim$0.8, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.18 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.10 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. It accurately reproduces the H I column density distribution function (CDDF) and the $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ relation, recovering CDDF slopes consistent with VIPER and a lower-envelope relation with an RMS difference of only 0.36 km s$^{-1}$. Applied to high-resolution UVES spectra, performance decreases to an F1 score of $\sim$0.5, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.34 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.21 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. Latent-space analysis reveals a significant domain shift between the simulated and observational spectra, contributing to the reduced performance. Nevertheless, the CNN preserves the observed CDDF and $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ distributions, yielding CDDF slopes consistent with VIPER and a lower-envelope RMS difference of 2.96 km s$^{-1}$. Monte Carlo dropout is implemented during inference to quantify predictive uncertainties. Together with its computational efficiency, the method provides a scalable and uncertainty-aware framework for Ly$α$ forest analysis in upcoming spectroscopic surveys.

AI.tldr: A CNN trained on IllustrisTNG synthetic spectra predicts Lyα absorber properties (N_HI, b_HI, centroid) directly from quasar spectra, achieving high accuracy on simulated data (F1~0.8) but moderate performance on real UVES spectra (F1~0.5) due to domain shift, while still recovering key statistical distributions (CDDF, b_HI-N_HI relation) with uncertainty quantification via Monte Carlo dropout.
AI.motivation: Traditional Voigt-profile fitting for Lyα forest analysis is computationally expensive; there is a need for a faster, scalable method to handle upcoming large spectroscopic surveys.
AI.method: Train a CNN on synthetic quasar spectra from IllustrisTNG simulations, using VIPER Voigt-profile fitting outputs as ground truth labels. The network jointly predicts absorber presence, log N_HI, log b_HI, and line centroid. Monte Carlo dropout provides uncertainty quantification.
AI.result: On simulated spectra: F1 ~0.8, MAE ~0.18 in log N_HI, ~0.10 in log b_HI; CDDF and b_HI-N_HI relation recovered accurately. On UVES spectra: F1 ~0.5, MAE ~0.34 in log N_HI, ~0.21 in log b_HI; domain shift degrades performance but statistical distributions are preserved.
AI.conclusion: The CNN offers a computationally efficient, uncertainty-aware alternative to Voigt-profile fitting for Lyα forest analysis, though domain shift between simulations and observations needs to be addressed for better real-data performance.

title: Analyzing Cosmic Ray Spectral Features: A Numerical Investigation
comment: 23 pages, 12 figures. Published in the Special Issue "Astrophysics of cosmic rays in the multi-messenger era"
summary: Recent cosmic ray space-based and balloon-borne experiments have revealed various spectral features. Spectral hardening around ~200 GV has been seen in primary nuclei as well as secondaries produced during propagation. Proton spectrum softening at ~10 TV and helium spectrum softening at a few tens TV has also been seen. Additionally, a positron excess has been observed above ~25 GeV. The cosmic ray propagation code, GALPROP v57, was utilized to investigate the cause behind these features. A diffusion model with reacceleration and convection effects was used as a baseline. To find the best fit to the experimental data, GALPROP v57's parameter optimization module, utilizing the external numerical minimization software MINUIT2, was used. For the hardening, three scenarios were studied: (1) a diffusion coefficient break, (2) injection spectra breaks, and (3) a combination of both breaks. An additional injection spectrum break was considered to fit the softening of the proton and helium spectra. An additional positron source was introduced for the positron excess. The resulting elemental spectra and ratios, along with the all-particle spectrum, are compared to compiled cosmic ray data. Implications of these spectral features are also discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper uses GALPROP v57 with MINUIT2 optimization to model cosmic ray spectral features: hardening at ~200 GV, proton/He softening at ~10-30 TV, and positron excess above ~25 GeV. Three scenarios (diffusion break, injection breaks, combination) are tested, with an additional positron source for the excess.
AI.motivation: To investigate the origin of recently observed cosmic ray spectral features (hardening, softening, positron excess) using a unified propagation framework.
AI.method: GALPROP v57 with parameter optimization via MINUIT2; baseline diffusion+reacceleration+convection model; three hardening scenarios (diffusion break, injection breaks, combined); additional injection break for proton/He softening; extra positron source for the excess.
AI.result: Elemental spectra, secondary-to-primary ratios, and all-particle spectrum compared to experimental data; best-fit scenarios identified for each spectral feature.
AI.conclusion: The spectral features can be reproduced through combinations of diffusion coefficient breaks, injection spectrum breaks, and an additional positron source, with implications for cosmic ray propagation and sources.

title: Non-spherical Cows: Introducing the Asphericity Parameter as a Measure of Accretion Geometry
comment: submitted to A&A
summary: The outer regions of galactic halos represent the bridge connecting internal processes within the galaxy to the larger surrounding cosmic web. The gas in this bridge region is shaped by the competing processes of cold inflows from the web and hot ejecta from feedback of supernovae or an active galactic nucleus. Similarly, the gas around galaxy clusters characterizes the balance between inflows and outflows. To study this connection, we introduce a new parameter for quantifying the geometrical configuration of the flow field connecting structures to the cosmic web, the asphericity parameter. This inflow asphericity is based on a spherical harmonics decomposition of the inflow at the virial boundary of the halo. It can be computed using both the linear and the logarithmic inflow field. To validate this parameter we apply it to both an extensive toy model set and to simulated haloes from the Magneticum simulations. We find the linear asphericity to be a tracer of the total power of the non-spherical inflow and the total anisotropy. On the other hand, the logarithmic asphericity traces the covering fraction of inflows at the surface and is highly sensitive to regions with zero inflow (regions that are dominated by outflow). Thus the asphericity of the flow field is a powerful tool to simultaneously study the geometry of in- and outflows in numerical simulations.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an "asphericity parameter" based on spherical harmonics decomposition to quantify the geometrical configuration of gas inflows at the virial boundary of galactic and cluster halos, validated using toy models and Magneticum simulations. Linear asphericity traces total inflow anisotropy, while logarithmic asphericity traces inflow covering fraction and is sensitive to outflow-dominated regions.
AI.motivation: To study the connection between galaxy/cluster halos and the cosmic web by quantifying the geometry of gas flows at halo boundaries, which are shaped by competing cold inflows from the cosmic web and hot outflows from feedback processes.
AI.method: A new asphericity parameter is introduced based on spherical harmonics decomposition of the inflow velocity field at the virial boundary, computed using both linear and logarithmic inflow fields. Validated on toy models and simulated halos from the Magneticum simulations.
AI.result: Linear asphericity traces the total power of non-spherical inflow and total anisotropy. Logarithmic asphericity traces the covering fraction of inflows at the surface and is highly sensitive to outflow-dominated regions (zero inflow).
AI.conclusion: The asphericity of the flow field is a powerful tool for simultaneously studying the geometry of in- and outflows in numerical simulations, linking internal galactic processes to the cosmic web.

title: Dependence of Particle Acceleration Efficiency on Shock Velocity in Weakly Magnetized Electron-Ion Shocks
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures
summary: Using unprecedentedly long 2D particle-in-cell simulations, we study electron and ion acceleration in weakly magnetized quasi-parallel shocks, propagating at velocities ranging from transrelativistic to subrelativistic. At a fixed upstream magnetic field strength, low-velocity quasi-parallel shocks are dominated by the Bell instability, whereas high-velocity shocks are dominated by the Weibel instability. Both regimes accelerate ions with similar efficiency, with the Bell-dominated regime exhibiting faster growth in the maximum particle energy. The electron acceleration efficiency is strongly dependent on shock velocity. Weibel-dominated shocks have $\sim15\,\%$ of shock energy in nonthermal electrons, whereas in the Bell-dominated regime we attribute less than $\sim2\,\%$ of shock energy to nonthermal electrons. We discuss applications of our results to the bright X-ray emission from the late-stage afterglows of gamma-ray bursts, the radio emission from fast blue optical transients, and the X-ray variability in microquasars.

AI.tldr: Using 2D particle-in-cell simulations, this paper studies particle acceleration in weakly magnetized quasi-parallel shocks, finding that Bell instability dominates low-velocity shocks while Weibel instability dominates high-velocity shocks. Both regimes accelerate ions similarly, but electron acceleration is much stronger in Weibel-dominated shocks (~15% shock energy) compared to Bell-dominated shocks (~2%). Results apply to GRB afterglows, fast blue optical transients, and microquasars.
AI.motivation: To understand electron and ion acceleration mechanisms in weakly magnetized quasi-parallel shocks across different velocity regimes, and to explain observed X-ray and radio emissions from astrophysical transients.
AI.method: Unprecedentedly long 2D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of weakly magnetized quasi-parallel shocks with velocities ranging from transrelativistic to subrelativistic.
AI.result: (1) Low-velocity shocks dominated by Bell instability; high-velocity shocks dominated by Weibel instability. (2) Ion acceleration efficiency similar in both regimes, but Bell-dominated regime shows faster growth in maximum particle energy. (3) Electron acceleration efficiency strongly velocity-dependent: ~15% shock energy in nonthermal electrons for Weibel-dominated shocks vs. ~2% for Bell-dominated shocks.
AI.conclusion: Different instability regimes govern particle acceleration depending on shock velocity, with important implications for understanding nonthermal emission from GRB afterglows, fast blue optical transients, and microquasars.

title: The tidal features of the classical Milky Way satellites: Expected in MOND but inconsistent with cold dark matter models
comment: 20 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Most classical satellites of the Milky Way are known to display signs of tidal disturbance (e.g. tidal tails, substructures, and distorted shapes). This cannot be explained by the standard model of cosmology due to its prediction that the dark matter haloes of the classical satellites confer them with very strong self-gravity and make them resilient to the Milky Way's gravitational tides. In this work, we estimate the tidal susceptibility of the classical satellites by comparing their half-mass radius with their theoretical tidal radius at pericentre in both the standard model and in the Milgromian dynamics (MOND) model. With this approach, we demonstrate that most classical satellites are expected to be tidally perturbed in MOND, so their observed tidal features are generally in good agreement with MOND expectations. Since gravitational tides can also enhance the velocity dispersion of the satellites, we argue that MOND can plausibly explain the unusually high velocity dispersions reported for some of the classical satellites.

AI.tldr: Classical Milky Way satellites show tidal disturbances that contradict standard cosmology predictions but align with MOND, which naturally explains their tidal features and elevated velocity dispersions.
AI.motivation: The observed tidal disturbances (tails, substructures, distorted shapes) in most classical Milky Way satellites cannot be explained by the standard cosmological model, which predicts that dark matter haloes make satellites resilient to tidal disruption.
AI.method: The authors estimate tidal susceptibility by comparing the half-mass radius with the theoretical tidal radius at pericentre for classical satellites in both the standard model and Milgromian dynamics (MOND).
AI.result: Most classical satellites are expected to be tidally perturbed in MOND, and their observed tidal features agree with MOND expectations. MOND can also plausibly explain the unusually high velocity dispersions reported for some satellites.
AI.conclusion: MOND provides a consistent framework for understanding the observed tidal disruption and kinematic properties of classical Milky Way satellites, whereas the standard dark matter model fails to account for these features.

title: Multi-messenger View of White Dwarf Tidal Disruption Events by Intermediate-Mass Black Holes: I. Gravitational Waves and Disk Photon and Neutrino Emissions
comment: 25 pages, 22 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: White dwarf (WD) tidal disruption events (TDEs) provide a unique window onto intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs). We present a multi-messenger view of these systems in two papers. In this paper, we develop an accretion-disk model for WD--TDEs in which the bound debris accretes at extremely super-Eddington rates, $\sim 10^5$--$10^9$ times higher than in typical (main-sequence) TDEs. The model includes magnetic pressure, nuclear-burning heating, wind mass loss, and neutrino production via $e^{\pm}$ pair annihilation. At such high accretion rates, the gas and radiation temperatures of the inner flow can reach $T\gtrsim 10^9\,\mathrm{K}$, enabling prolific pair production and MeV neutrino emission. We find that the disk is predominantly advection dominated over a broad range of accretion rates, while disk winds can partially cool the flow and reduce the inner temperature. The predicted thermal EM emission is nearly insensitive to the fallback rate in the super-Eddington regime: the luminosity only mildly exceeds the IMBH Eddington luminosity and the spectrum peaks at $\sim 0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{keV}$, implying detectability with current X-ray facilities such as Einstein Probe. For low-mass IMBHs ($\sim 10^3\,M_{\odot}$), the disk can also produce a burst of MeV neutrinos with luminosities up to $\sim 10^{47}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ for ONeMg WD--TDEs, although detectability with current neutrino detectors (e.g., Super-Kamiokande and JUNO) is limited to Galactic distances. Finally, we estimate the GW burst produced during the final passage prior to disruption, which peaks at $\sim 0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, placing WD--TDEs in the target band of proposed decihertz detectors and motivating coordinated GW+EM+neutrino searches. We also present a first exploration of GWs from a precessing WD--TDE disk; this signal is much weaker, with a detection horizon $\lesssim 1\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ for these missions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an accretion-disk model for white dwarf tidal disruption events around intermediate-mass black holes, finding extreme super-Eddington accretion rates produce MeV neutrino emission, thermal X-ray emission detectable by Einstein Probe, and gravitational wave signals in the decihertz band, motivating multi-messenger searches.
AI.motivation: White dwarf TDEs provide a unique window onto intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs), which are poorly understood. The extreme accretion physics of these events has not been thoroughly modeled, and their multi-messenger signatures (EM, neutrinos, GWs) remain unexplored.
AI.method: The authors develop an accretion-disk model for WD-TDEs at super-Eddington rates (~10⁵–10⁹ times Eddington), incorporating magnetic pressure, nuclear burning, wind mass loss, and neutrino production via e± pair annihilation. They also estimate gravitational wave signals from the final orbital passage and precessing disk.
AI.result: The disk is advection-dominated; thermal EM luminosity mildly exceeds Eddington and peaks at ~0.1–1 keV, detectable by Einstein Probe. For low-mass IMBHs (~10³ M⊙), ONeMg WD-TDEs produce MeV neutrino bursts up to ~10⁴⁷ erg/s, detectable only within Galactic distances. GWs from the final passage peak at ~0.1–1 Hz (decihertz band), while precessing disk GWs are much weaker (horizon <1 Mpc).
AI.conclusion: WD-TDEs are promising multi-messenger sources for studying IMBHs, with detectable X-ray emission from current facilities, MeV neutrinos for nearby events, and gravitational waves motivating decihertz detectors and coordinated EM+GW+neutrino searches.

title: Warped Disk Galaxies: Alignment with the Large-Scale Tidal Field
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures. Comments are welcome
summary: A possible origin of disk galaxy warps is the misalignment between galactic disks and their host dark matter halos, the orientations of which are found to be statistically aligned with the large-scale tidal field. In this work, we test this scenario by examining the alignment between warped disk galaxies and the large-scale tidal field reconstructed from the ELUCID project. We find a statistically significant alignment signal between disk orientations and the $t_1$ direction, with warped and non-warped galaxies showing different alignment behaviors. Warped galaxies show an excess of intermediate angles and a preference for orientations slightly offset from perfect parallel and perpendicular alignments. In contrast, non-warped galaxies exhibit a deficit of intermediate angles relative to random expectations, which becomes more pronounced after matching to a control sample. We also find a clear mass dependence, with high-mass warped galaxies contributing the excess of intermediate-angle signal. No significant alignment signal in warped galaxies is detected with the $t_3$ direction.

AI.tldr: This study tests whether disk galaxy warps originate from misalignment with dark matter halos by examining alignment between warped galaxies and the large-scale tidal field from the ELUCID project. Warped galaxies show excess intermediate angles and slight offsets from perfect alignments with the t1 direction, especially at high masses, while non-warped galaxies show a deficit of intermediate angles. No significant alignment with t3 is found.
AI.motivation: To test the scenario that disk galaxy warps originate from misalignment between galactic disks and their host dark matter halos, whose orientations are statistically aligned with the large-scale tidal field.
AI.method: Using the ELUCID project to reconstruct the large-scale tidal field, the authors examine the alignment between warped disk galaxies and the tidal field directions (t1 and t3), comparing warped versus non-warped galaxies, and analyzing mass dependence.
AI.result: Warped galaxies show excess intermediate angles and slight offsets from perfect parallel/perpendicular alignments with t1; non-warped galaxies show a deficit of intermediate angles. High-mass warped galaxies drive the excess intermediate-angle signal. No significant alignment with t3 is detected.
AI.conclusion: The distinct alignment behaviors of warped vs. non-warped galaxies with the large-scale tidal field support the scenario that disk warps are linked to misalignment with dark matter halos, with a clear mass dependence.

title: Unveiling the Local Environment of FRB 20220912A: Sub-arcsecond $4-26$ GHz Radio Continuum Mapping
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables
summary: The local environments of repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide critical clues to their progenitors. While some active repeaters (e.g., FRB~20121102A, FRB~20190520B) are embedded in compact persistent radio sources (PRS), others appear to reside in cleaner environments. We present a high-resolution, multi-frequency (4$-$26 GHz) continuum study of the hyperactive repeater FRB 20220912A using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA). We report the discovery of a previously unknown radio source distinct from the compact PRSs seen in other FRBs, spatially coincident with the FRB position and offset by $\approx 300$~mas ($\approx 450$~pc) from the host galaxy's center. The absence of continuum emission in archival milliarcsecond-resolution VLBI observations indicates that the source is resolved out, ruling out a hyper-compact ($< 1$~pc) central-engine-powered origin. We constrain the physical diameter of the emitting region between 75~pc and 190~pc. We further demonstrate that the source is characterized by a steep non-thermal spectral index ($α\approx -0.73$) and a remarkably high star-formation rate surface density $Σ_{\text{SFR}} \gtrsim 13~M_{\odot}~\text{yr}^{-1}~\text{kpc}^{-2}$. We argue that this emission is best explained as a compact star-forming region within the host galaxy. This association with a site of ongoing star formation provides strong observational support for the hypothesis that young magnetars, formed after the deaths of massive stars, are the progenitors of at least some repeating FRBs.

AI.tldr: High-resolution VLA observations of FRB 20220912A reveal a compact, steep-spectrum radio source (~75–190 pc) offset from its host galaxy center, consistent with a star-forming region rather than a compact persistent radio source (PRS). This supports young magnetars formed from massive star deaths as progenitors of some repeating FRBs.
AI.motivation: Local environments of repeating FRBs provide critical clues to their progenitors. While some active repeaters are embedded in compact PRS, others appear to reside in cleaner environments, motivating a detailed study of FRB 20220912A's surroundings.
AI.method: High-resolution, multi-frequency (4–26 GHz) VLA continuum observations of the hyperactive repeater FRB 20220912A, combined with archival VLBI data to constrain source size and morphology.
AI.result: Discovery of a radio source offset ~300 mas (~450 pc) from the host galaxy center. VLBI non-detection rules out hyper-compact (<1 pc) central-engine origin. Physical diameter constrained to 75–190 pc. Steep non-thermal spectral index (α ≈ −0.73) and high star-formation rate surface density (Σ_SFR ≳ 13 M⊙ yr⁻¹ kpc⁻²).
AI.conclusion: The emission is best explained as a compact star-forming region within the host galaxy, providing strong observational support for young magnetars (formed after massive star deaths) as progenitors of at least some repeating FRBs.

title: Globular cluster abundance patterns inherited from giant molecular clouds
comment: Submitted. 4 main figures, 7 extended data figures
summary: Globular clusters exhibit large star-to-star variations and anticorrelations in their light element abundances that are commonly interpreted in terms of in-cluster self-enrichment, in which ejecta from early-forming cluster stars pollute the gas from which later stars form over millions of years. Yet proposed self-enrichment scenarios suffer from a severe mass-budget problem or invoke exotic stellar populations. Using cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations with a standard chemical enrichment model, we identify a population of giant molecular clouds whose internal abundance patterns reproduce several key globular cluster signatures: large light-element abundance spreads and nitrogen-oxygen anticorrelations at nearly constant iron abundance. These clouds form at the restart of star-formation activity after an earlier starburst, where previously ejected oxygen-rich gas collides with nitrogen-rich galactic gas, and are sites of dense star-cluster formation. In this picture, the chemical abundance patterns of globular clusters need not require extended in-cluster star formation, but can be inherited at birth from chemically structured interstellar gas shaped by the baryon cycle. Globular clusters therefore provide a fossil record of chemical enrichment and gas flows in high-redshift galaxies.

AI.tldr: Using cosmological simulations, the paper shows that globular cluster chemical abundance patterns (light-element variations, N-O anticorrelations, constant iron) can be inherited from chemically structured interstellar gas formed by the baryon cycle, rather than requiring extended in-cluster self-enrichment.
AI.motivation: To resolve the mass-budget problem in self-enrichment scenarios for globular cluster abundance anomalies and to avoid invoking exotic stellar populations.
AI.method: Cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations with a standard chemical enrichment model were used to identify giant molecular clouds whose internal abundance patterns match key globular cluster signatures.
AI.result: A population of giant molecular clouds was found that reproduces large light-element abundance spreads and N-O anticorrelations at nearly constant iron abundance. These form at the restart of star formation after an earlier starburst, where oxygen-rich ejecta collide with nitrogen-rich galactic gas.
AI.conclusion: Globular cluster chemical patterns can be inherited at birth from chemically structured interstellar gas shaped by the baryon cycle, not requiring extended in-cluster star formation. GCs serve as fossil records of chemical enrichment and gas flows in high-redshift galaxies.

title: Identifying a circum-jet southern ring counterpart to the northern jet of the Crab Nebula
comment: Accepted for publication in Research Notes of the AAS
summary: I analyze images of the Crab Nebula core-collapse supernova (CCSN) remnant in light of recent three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) and identify a southern ring opposite to the northern jet, which I attribute to a counterjet. The Crab Nebula is known for its point-symmetric morphology of seven pairs of bays and a pair of two filaments, but no pairs of two jets or their direct outcomes, like ears and rings, have been identified. I identify a ring in visible and infrared images of the Crab Nebula opposite to the prominent northern jet. Recent hydrodynamical simulations of the JJEM show that jets that explode CCSNe can form such circum-jet rings. I, therefore, attribute the shaping of the southern ring to a southern jet, a counter jet to the northern jet, both of which participated in the explosion of the Crab Nebula in the framework of the JJEM.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a southern ring in the Crab Nebula as a counterjet to the northern jet, supporting the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) for the supernova based on 3D hydrodynamical simulations.
AI.motivation: To find evidence for the JJEM in the Crab Nebula by identifying a counterjet opposite to the known northern jet, as no pairs of jets or their direct outcomes had been previously identified.
AI.method: Analysis of visible and infrared images of the Crab Nebula paired with comparisons to recent three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of the JJEM.
AI.result: A southern ring is identified opposite to the northern jet, matching simulation predictions of circum-jet rings formed by counterjets in the JJEM.
AI.conclusion: The southern ring is attributed to a southern counterjet that participated in the Crab Nebula's explosion, providing observational support for the JJEM framework.

title: Constraints on the population level distribution of nearby Dark Matter halo shapes with extragalactic streams
summary: Stellar streams trace the gravitational potential of their host galaxies and provide a sensitive probe of dark matter halo structure. Previously, we developed, and tested on simulated data, a hierarchical Bayesian framework to infer the population level distribution of dark matter halo shapes from ensembles of extragalactic stellar streams with images only. In this work, we apply this pipeline to 32 stellar streams from the STRRINGS catalogue, a curated sample of dynamically cold minor-merger streams detected in deep imaging. Each stream is forward-modelled assuming an axisymmetric halo and fitted using only the projected stream track, yielding posterior constraints on the halo flattening parameter $q$. To account for model mismatch and track systematics, we introduce an additional variance term that inflates the uncertainty on the projected stream track and use it to identify a high quality (gold) subsample of 17 streams whose tracks retain significant constraining power. We then combine the individual posteriors through importance sampling to infer the underlying population distribution of halo flattening. For the \textit{gold} subsample, we infer an oblate population with mean $μ_q \approx 0.72$ and intrinsic scatter $σ_q \approx 0.34$. Streams dominated by additional model variance yield a nearly spherical population inference. The inferred oblate population for the gold sample is broadly consistent with expectations from cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. This work provides constraints on dark matter halo flattening from stellar streams beyond the Local Group and establishes a scalable framework for forthcoming large samples from Euclid and Rubin/LSST.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical Bayesian framework is applied to 32 extragalactic stellar streams from the STRRINGS catalogue to infer dark matter halo flattening, finding an oblate population (mean q≈0.72, scatter≈0.34) from a high-quality gold subsample of 17 streams, consistent with cosmological simulations.
AI.motivation: To infer dark matter halo shapes from extragalactic stellar streams beyond the Local Group, moving beyond previous simulation-only tests and establishing a scalable approach for future large surveys.
AI.method: Forward-modelled 32 stellar streams assuming axisymmetric halos, fitted projected stream tracks via hierarchical Bayesian inference, used additional variance term for model mismatch, identified gold subsample (17 streams), combined posteriors via importance sampling for population-level distribution.
AI.result: Gold subsample: oblate population with mean μ_q≈0.72, intrinsic scatter σ_q≈0.34; streams with additional model variance yield nearly spherical inference; consistent with cosmological hydrodynamical simulations.
AI.conclusion: Provides first constraints on dark matter halo flattening from extragalactic stellar streams beyond the Local Group, and establishes a scalable framework for future large samples from Euclid and Rubin/LSST.

title: Two fluid CFL strange quark stars with scalar dark matter: critical mass and mass gap implications
comment: 23 pages, 20 figures, 8 tables
summary: We investigate the structure of strange quark stars (SQSs) in the color--flavor--locked (CFL) phase in the presence of scalar bosonic dark matter within a two--fluid formalism employing perturbative QCD. By considering different dark matter masses and varying the pairing gap $Δ$ and {the central dark matter pressure fraction} $f_r$, we analyze the impact of dark matter on the structural properties of SQSs, including the maximum gravitational mass $M_{\mathrm{TOV}}$, the ratio of dark matter to strange-quark-matter radii $R_{\mathrm{DM}}/R_{\mathrm{SQM}}$, and the dimensionless tidal deformability $Λ$. We further examine the compatibility of the resulting mass--radius relations with the recent NICER measurements of compact stars. Within the parameter space considered in this study, we find that $M_{\mathrm{TOV}}$ exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the dark matter mass, with a critical value beyond which $M_{\mathrm{TOV}}$ decreases. We also show that some pure CFL strange quark star configurations, particularly those associated with very stiff EOSs and larger maximum masses, may not simultaneously remain compatible with the $Λ$ range inferred from GW170817 while occupying the lower mass--gap region. In contrast, the inclusion of dark matter allows two-fluid CFL strange quark star configurations to reproduce the observed properties of massive compact objects in the lower mass--gap region, such as the secondary component of GW190814, while remaining qualitatively compatible with the $Λ$ range inferred from GW170817. We note, however, that the GW170817 constraints were originally inferred within single-fluid compact-star frameworks and therefore provide only {qualitative guidance} for the present two-fluid halo configurations. Our results suggest that exotic compact-star configurations may populate part of the conventionally defined lower mass--gap region.

AI.tldr: This paper studies strange quark stars in the color-flavor-locked phase with scalar bosonic dark matter using a two-fluid formalism. It finds non-monotonic dependence of maximum mass on dark matter mass and shows that dark matter allows configurations to satisfy constraints from GW170817 and GW190814, suggesting exotic compact stars may occupy the lower mass-gap region.
AI.motivation: To investigate how scalar bosonic dark matter affects the structural properties of CFL strange quark stars, and to examine whether such two-fluid configurations can explain observed compact objects in the lower mass-gap region (e.g., the secondary component of GW190814) while remaining compatible with tidal deformability constraints from GW170817.
AI.method: Two-fluid formalism within perturbative QCD, considering different dark matter masses, pairing gap Δ, and central dark matter pressure fraction f_r. Structural properties (maximum gravitational mass, radius ratio, tidal deformability) are computed and compared with NICER and GW170817/GW190814 constraints.
AI.result: Maximum mass M_TOV shows non-monotonic dependence on dark matter mass with a critical value. Pure CFL SQSs with stiff EOSs may conflict with GW170817 Λ constraints in the lower mass-gap region. Including dark matter allows two-fluid CFL configurations to reproduce observed properties of massive compact objects in the lower mass-gap region while remaining qualitatively compatible with GW170817 constraints.
AI.conclusion: Exotic compact-star configurations (CFL strange quark stars with dark matter) may populate part of the conventionally defined lower mass-gap region, and GW170817 constraints provide only qualitative guidance for two-fluid halo configurations since they were originally inferred for single-fluid frameworks.

title: The problem of escape: a missing bit in the theory of the origin of cosmic rays
comment: Short Review to appear in "Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences"
summary: The escape of cosmic rays from their sources, as well as from the region surrounding a source, or from the galaxy hosting the sources, is a non-linear process that involves a complex chain of events, often overlooked. On the other hand, these phenomena are responsible for setting the maximum energy in accelerators, shaping the source spectra and determining the conditions for escape from the galaxy hosting the sources, a process that is usually modeled by imposing ad hoc boundary conditions in our equations. Here we discuss some of these phenomena and how they affect the spectra of cosmic rays measured at the Earth.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the non-linear escape processes of cosmic rays from sources, surrounding regions, and host galaxies, and how these phenomena affect the spectra measured at Earth.
AI.motivation: The escape of cosmic rays from their sources and host galaxies is a non-linear process often overlooked or oversimplified with ad hoc boundary conditions.
AI.method: The paper discusses various phenomena involved in the non-linear chain of cosmic ray escape processes.
AI.result: The paper describes how these phenomena shape source spectra, set maximum energy in accelerators, and determine escape conditions from host galaxies.
AI.conclusion: The escape processes significantly affect the spectra of cosmic rays measured at Earth.

title: Survival is not Enough: Dust Sputtering, Growth, and H$_2$ Formation in Galactic Winds
comment: Submitted. Comments welcome. 22 pages, 16 figures
summary: A substantial amount of dust is found in galactic halos extending far beyond the disks, the origin of which remains an open question. Closely linked and equally puzzling is the detection of molecular gas in high-velocity galactic winds. To address this, we present the first cloud-crushing simulations that self-consistently include non-equilibrium cooling and chemistry with dust growth and sputtering. We find that surviving clouds naturally develop a two-phase structure, with a cold ($\sim 30$ K), dense core embedded in a warm ($\sim 10^4$ K), diffuse envelope. However, the presence of a cold phase does not always lead to molecular winds. While dust initially in the cloud largely survives in $10^6$ K winds, it is severely depleted by sputtering in hotter winds ($\gtrsim 10^7$ K). Importantly, without dust growth, the dust-to-gas ratio (DGR) of the cloud declines rapidly, suppressing the formation of molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) and keeping the entrained cloud atomic, even in cases where the majority of the initial dust survives. Nonthermal sputtering plays a subdominant role in all cases. The entrained clouds develop high molecular fractions only when dust growth is enabled, provided the cloud densities are sufficiently high ($\gtrsim$ 10 - 30 times the critical density for cloud survival). Our results suggest that "in situ" dust growth is essential to explain both the observed abundance of halo dust and the molecular gas in galactic winds.

AI.tldr: The paper uses cloud-crushing simulations with non-equilibrium cooling, chemistry, dust growth, and sputtering to show that entrained galactic halo clouds can develop molecular gas only when in situ dust growth is enabled at sufficiently high densities, explaining both observed halo dust abundances and molecular gas in galactic winds.
AI.motivation: To address two open questions: (1) the origin of substantial dust found in galactic halos far beyond disks, and (2) the detection of molecular gas in high-velocity galactic winds.
AI.method: First cloud-crushing simulations that self-consistently include non-equilibrium cooling and chemistry with dust growth and sputtering.
AI.result: Surviving clouds develop a two-phase structure (cold ~30 K core, warm ~10^4 K envelope). Dust survives in 10^6 K winds but is depleted by sputtering in hotter (>10^7 K) winds. Without dust growth, DGR declines rapidly, suppressing H₂ formation. High molecular fractions only occur with dust growth at sufficiently high densities (>10-30 times critical density for survival). Nonthermal sputtering is subdominant.
AI.conclusion: In situ dust growth is essential to explain both the observed abundance of halo dust and molecular gas in galactic winds.

title: A Possible Triple Formation Scenario of Binary Black Hole Merge With One In Pair-instability Supernova Mass Gap
comment: 13 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to Physical Review D
summary: Observations of binary black hole (BBH) mergers detected by LIGO -- such as GW170729, GW190620, GW190706, GW230107, GW230820, and GW230928 -- feature high effective spins and primary black holes that fall squarely into the pair-instability supernova (PISN) mass gap ($\sim 45-130 \, M_{\odot}$). These events pose a significant challenge to standard stellar and binary evolution theories. To address this, we propose an isolated hierarchical triple stellar evolution channel. In this framework, tidal synchronization in tight inner binaries drives chemically homogeneous evolution (CHE), entirely bypassing giant expansion. A subsequent triple common envelope (TCE) evolution, triggered by the tertiary companion, rapidly drives the inner BBH to coalescence. Our model can provide a detailed evolutionary pathway that elegantly reproduces the properties of these GWs, such as GW190706. Assuming a low-metallicity environment ($Z = 0.001$), our framework predicts a volumetric merger rate of approximately $0.011 \, \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ at $z \approx 0.68$, accounting for $22\%$ of the empirical rate for this mass regime in the GWTC-4 catalog. This study demonstrates that primordial triple interactions are a highly efficient avenue for populating the PISN mass gap.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an isolated hierarchical triple stellar evolution channel to explain BBH mergers detected by LIGO that fall into the PISN mass gap (~45–130 M⊙) and feature high effective spins. Tidal synchronization in tight inner binaries drives chemically homogeneous evolution (CHE), bypassing giant expansion, and a subsequent triple common envelope (TCE) evolution triggers inner BBH coalescence. The model reproduces event properties (e.g., GW190706) and predicts a merger rate of ~0.011 Gpc⁻³yr⁻¹ at z≈0.68, accounting for 22% of the empirical rate in GWTC-4.
AI.motivation: Observed LIGO BBH mergers (e.g., GW170729, GW190620, GW190706, GW230107, GW230820, GW230928) have high effective spins and primary black holes within the PISN mass gap (~45–130 M⊙), challenging standard stellar and binary evolution theories.
AI.method: The authors propose an isolated hierarchical triple stellar evolution channel: (1) tidal synchronization in tight inner binaries drives chemically homogeneous evolution (CHE), bypassing giant expansion; (2) a triple common envelope (TCE) evolution triggered by the tertiary companion rapidly drives the inner BBH to coalescence.
AI.result: The model reproduces properties of events like GW190706. Assuming low metallicity (Z=0.001), it predicts a volumetric merger rate of ~0.011 Gpc⁻³yr⁻¹ at z≈0.68, contributing ~22% of the empirical rate for this mass regime in GWTC-4.
AI.conclusion: Primordial triple interactions are a highly efficient avenue for populating the PISN mass gap, providing a viable channel for the formation of these puzzling BBH mergers.

authors: The SKA Pulsar Science Working Group
title: Exploring the Galactic plasma with pulsars in the SKA Era
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026. Report-no:AASKAII/Tiburzi01
summary: The ionised media that permeate the Milky Way have been active topics of research since the discovery of pulsars in 1967. In fact, pulsars allow one to study several aspects of said plasma, such as their column density, turbulence, scattering measures, and discrete, intervening structures between the neutron star and the observer, and aspects of the magnetic field throughout. Such sources of information allow us to characterise the electron distribution in the terrestrial ionosphere, the Solar Wind, and our Galaxy and have an important impact on other experiments involving pulsars such as Pulsar Timing Arrays. In this article, we review the state-of-the-art of plasma research using pulsars, the aspects that should be taken into consideration for optimal plasma studies, and we provide future perspectives on improvements to those enabled by the SKA.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews how pulsars enable the study of ionised media in the Milky Way, including electron column density, turbulence, scattering, magnetic fields, and discrete intervening structures, covering environments from the ionosphere to the Solar Wind and the Galaxy, and discusses implications for Pulsar Timing Arrays and future prospects with the SKA.
AI.motivation: Since the discovery of pulsars in 1967, the ionised media permeating the Milky Way have been actively studied; pulsars provide unique probes of plasma properties including column density, turbulence, scattering, magnetic fields, and discrete structures between the neutron star and observer.
AI.method: This is a review article that synthesises the state-of-the-art in plasma research using pulsars, discussing observational techniques and considerations for optimal plasma studies.
AI.result: Pulsars enable characterisation of electron distribution across the ionosphere, Solar Wind, and Galactic medium, with important impacts on Pulsar Timing Arrays and other pulsar-based experiments.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides future perspectives on improvements to plasma studies enabled by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA).

title: Deep far-UV observations of the ELAIS N1 field using AstroSat: Source catalogue, spectral energy distribution modelling and star formation
comment: 11 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publishing in MNRAS
summary: We present a far-ultraviolet (FUV) photometric study of the ELAIS N1 deep field using the Ultra-Violet Imaging Telescope (UVIT) onboard AstroSat, observed in the F154W filter ($λ_{\rm eff} = 1541$\,Å) with a total on-source exposure time of 30\,ksec. Level 1 data were reduced using CCDLAB v3.0, yielding source catalogues of 1637 objects at $3σ$ and 458 objects at $5σ$, with limiting magnitudes of $25.69\,m_{AB}$ and $25.13\,m_{AB}$ respectively. FUV positions are cross-matched against multiwavelength catalogues spanning optical and infrared wavelengths, with redshifts drawn from spectroscopic and photometric sources. Active galactic nuclei (AGN) are identified and excluded via established multiwavelength criteria, leaving a clean sample of star-forming galaxies (SFGs). Spectral energy distribution (SED) modelling is performed using CIGALE, employing a delayed star formation history with an optional late burst, Bruzual \& Charlot stellar population synthesis, Calzetti dust attenuation, and the SKIRTOR AGN module. From the best-fit models, we derive star formation rates (SFRs), total stellar masses, and young stellar masses as a function of redshift. The SFR increases monotonically with redshift, consistent with the evolution of the Star Formation Main Sequence (SFMS). The ratio of young-to-total stellar mass remains approximately constant across $0 < z \lesssim 0.76$, confirming that the sample consists predominantly of secularly evolving systems undergoing steady, self-regulated star formation rather than starburst-driven episodes.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a far-ultraviolet photometric study of the ELAIS N1 deep field using UVIT/AstroSat (F154W filter, 30 ksec exposure). Source catalogues of 1637 (3σ) and 458 (5σ) objects were produced, with limiting magnitudes of 25.69 m_AB and 25.13 m_AB. After cross-matching with multiwavelength data and excluding AGN via established criteria, a clean sample of star-forming galaxies was obtained. SED modelling with CIGALE (delayed SFH, Bruzual & Charlot, Calzetti dust, SKIRTOR AGN) yielded SFRs and stellar masses. SFR increases with redshift, consistent with the SFMS. The young-to-total stellar mass ratio is roughly constant over 0<z≲0.76, indicating secular, self-regulated star formation rather than starbursts.
AI.motivation: To conduct a deep FUV photometric study of the ELAIS N1 field using UVIT/AstroSat, derive SFRs and stellar masses for star-forming galaxies, and investigate the evolution of the star formation main sequence and the nature (secular vs. starburst) of star formation across redshift.
AI.method: FUV observations with UVIT/AstroSat (F154W filter, 30 ksec exposure); data reduction with CCDLAB v3.0; source extraction at 3σ and 5σ; cross-matching with multiwavelength optical/IR catalogues; AGN identification and exclusion using established multiwavelength criteria; SED modelling with CIGALE using delayed SFH + optional late burst, Bruzual & Charlot stellar population synthesis, Calzetti dust attenuation, and SKIRTOR AGN module.
AI.result: Catalogues of 1637 (3σ) and 458 (5σ) FUV sources with limiting magnitudes 25.69 m_AB and 25.13 m_AB; SFR increases monotonically with redshift, consistent with SFMS evolution; young-to-total stellar mass ratio approximately constant across 0<z≲0.76.
AI.conclusion: The sample consists predominantly of secularly evolving systems undergoing steady, self-regulated star formation rather than starburst-driven episodes.

title: Low-Frequency Recombination Lines from Galaxies and AGN over Cosmic Time
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Emig01
summary: Radio recombination lines (RRLs) at low frequencies (<10 GHz) can provide a multi-phase view of interstellar gas in nearby galaxies, absorption-line-systems, and AGN. Hydrogen RRLs arise in fully ionized gas and carbon RRLs trace elusive cold-HI and CO-dark molecular gas. Low frequency RRLs are typically stimulated by the radio continuum and thus may be observable within or against radio bright sources out to cosmological distances (z ~ 6). Although long sought after, RRLs were only recently detected outside of the local universe (z ~ 1; Emig et al., 2020, 2023). Such detections have been made possible by the advancement of wide-bandwidth spectral-line surveys on next-generation low-frequency telescopes. Precursors and pathfinders to the SKA have opened up this field of research and will make significant advancements over the next years by enabling surveys over large source samples. The SKA will provide access to the crucial frequency ranges where RRL line intensity is brightest. Furthermore, multi-band SKA measurements will fully characterize gas physical conditions. Key extragalactic science of low frequency RRLs will focus on (i) the conversion of baryonic material into stars across cosmic time, (ii) the evolution of the ISM and its physical conditions in galaxies, and (iii) how gas drives and inhibits AGN activity.

AI.tldr: Low-frequency radio recombination lines (RRLs) provide a multi-phase view of interstellar gas and can be observed at cosmological distances. Recent wide-bandwidth surveys with SKA pathfinders enabled first extragalactic RRL detections beyond the local universe. The SKA will fully characterize gas conditions and advance studies of star formation, ISM evolution, and AGN gas fueling across cosmic time.
AI.motivation: Low-frequency RRLs can probe multi-phase interstellar gas (ionized gas via H RRLs, cold-HI and CO-dark molecular gas via C RRLs) at cosmological distances, but were historically undetected beyond the local universe until recently. Wide-bandwidth surveys on next-generation telescopes finally enabled such detections.
AI.method: Wide-bandwidth spectral-line surveys using low-frequency telescopes (SKA precursors and pathfinders) detect radio continuum-stimulated RRLs at <10 GHz, enabling observations within or against radio-bright sources.
AI.result: First extragalactic RRL detections at z~1 achieved by Emig et al. (2020, 2023). SKA pathfinders enable surveys over large source samples, and the SKA will access the brightest RRL frequency ranges with multi-band measurements.
AI.conclusion: Low-frequency RRL science with the SKA will focus on three key areas: (i) baryonic star formation across cosmic time, (ii) ISM evolution and physical conditions in galaxies, and (iii) gas-driven AGN activity regulation.

title: The X-ray Variability of the Ultraluminous X-ray Sources in the NGC 4631 galaxy
summary: We perform a systematic study on the long-term X-ray variability for the five ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) in the NGC 4631 galaxy (X1-X5), using Chandra, XMM-Newton, and Swift observations covering a 24-year span. Light curves for the five ULXs are presented, while X-ray spectra were modeled for observations with sufficient counts. The normalized excess variance and structure function are utilized to study the X-ray variability behavior of the ULXs. The normalized excess variance is anti-correlated with average X-ray luminosity for three ULXs, indicating that objects with higher average luminosity tend to exhibit relatively lower amplitude of variability. The structure function values increases with time interval in two sources, showing that flux variations become more significant for longer timescales. These trends are also found in the X-ray variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs). The similarity between ULXs and AGNs, if confirmed for a larger sample of sources, possibly indicates similar underlying physical mechanisms for their X-ray variability.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes 24 years of X-ray observations of five ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) in NGC 4631, finding that their variability patterns (anti-correlation between excess variance and luminosity, increasing structure function with timescale) resemble those of AGNs, suggesting similar underlying physics.
AI.motivation: To systematically study the long-term X-ray variability properties of five ULXs in NGC 4631 and compare them with AGN variability patterns to explore potential common physical mechanisms.
AI.method: Light curves and X-ray spectra were obtained from Chandra, XMM-Newton, and Swift data over 24 years. Normalized excess variance and structure function analyses were applied to quantify variability behavior.
AI.result: Three ULXs show an anti-correlation between normalized excess variance and average X-ray luminosity. Two sources exhibit increasing structure function values with longer time intervals. These trends mirror those observed in AGN X-ray variability.
AI.conclusion: The similarity in variability patterns between ULXs and AGNs suggests possible common physical mechanisms for X-ray variability, pending confirmation with larger source samples.

title: An intrinsic decline of accretion activity in GRS 1915+105
comment: Submitted 2026 July 06. Comments welcome
summary: The canonical microquasar GRS 1915+105 is exhibiting unprecedented changes in its multiwavelength properties since 2018. Recent pointed observations with NuSTAR in November 2025 have failed to detect the source at flux limits several orders of magnitude deeper than historical X-ray levels. Under an enhanced obscuration scenario, the absence of hard X-rays requires that any obscuring cocoon must be deeply Compton-thick and fully sky covering, with a stringent limit on scattering fractions being less than 1 part in >~10^4, if intrinsic accretion activity continues unabated. An ionised cocoon could also account for a deep radio non-detection in June 2026. But such an interpretation is in conflict with mid-infrared fading of the source observed with SPHEREx in September 2025 and then again in April/May 2026. These facts, together with the source location in the infrared vs. X-ray plane, are consistent with an intrinsic weakening of accretion activity around November 2025 or earlier. We propose that outflows witnessed during intense multiwavelength flaring in 2023-2024 have progressively expelled fueling material from the inner disc, resulting in a significant drop in accretion activity. If correct, the current state gives unique insight into ongoing dramatic secular accretion changes on human timescales. High-frequency resolved radio observations and sensitive infrared or sub-mm observations could test this scenario, and characterise any gaseous cocoon still veiling the source.

AI.tldr: GRS 1915+105 has undergone dramatic changes since 2018, with NuSTAR non-detections in Nov 2025 requiring extreme Compton-thick obscuration; however, mid-IR fading observed by SPHEREx contradicts a pure obscuration scenario, suggesting instead an intrinsic shutdown of accretion activity due to progressive disc evacuation by outflows from 2023-2024 flaring.
AI.motivation: To understand the unprecedented multiwavelength transformation of the canonical microquasar GRS 1915+105 observed since 2018, characterized by extreme X-ray dimming and radio non-detections.
AI.method: Multiwavelength analysis combining NuSTAR (hard X-ray), SPHEREx (mid-infrared), and radio observations, testing two scenarios: enhanced obscuration (Compton-thick cocoon) vs. intrinsic accretion shutdown.
AI.result: NuSTAR non-detection requires a deeply Compton-thick, fully sky-covering cocoon with scattering fraction <10^-4, but this is inconsistent with SPHEREx mid-IR fading. The source's location in the infrared vs. X-ray plane favors intrinsic weakening of accretion starting around Nov 2025 or earlier.
AI.conclusion: Outflows from 2023-2024 flaring likely expelled inner disc fueling material, causing a dramatic drop in accretion activity. High-frequency radio and sensitive infrared/sub-mm observations are needed to test this scenario and characterize any remaining gaseous cocoon.

title: SN 2022erq: A Superluminous Thermonuclear Supernova with Escalating Pre-Explosion Mass Loss
comment: 28 pages, 18 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present a photometric and spectroscopic study of the superluminous Type Ia supernova SN 2022erq. Its early spectra, dominated by iron-group elements with weak intermediate-mass features, might indicate highly efficient nuclear burning, broadly similar to that inferred for some overluminous SNe Ia. The rapid emergence and persistence of narrow Balmer emission lines superposed on this iron-rich spectrum provide clear evidence of long-lived interaction with a hydrogen-rich circumstellar medium (CSM), establishing SN 2022erq as a member of the rare Ia-CSM class. SN 2022erq reached a peak bolometric luminosity of about 8 x 10^43 erg/s and exhibited an exceptionally slow post-peak decline, indicating that its light curve is dominated by long-duration ejecta-CSM interaction. By combining H-alpha diagnostics with bolometric light-curve modeling, we reconstruct the pre-explosion mass-loss history of the progenitor. The mass-loss rate escalated by one order of magnitude over the final decades, rising from about 0.04 to about 0.6 solar masses per year. This surge produced a massive, extended CSM shell of about 3 solar masses out to about 3.5 x 10^16 cm. The young stellar environment (about 100 Myr) together with this substantial, extensive CSM points to a progenitor system consisting of a white dwarf and an intermediate-mass companion that underwent increasing mass loss prior to explosion.

AI.tldr: SN 2022erq is a superluminous Type Ia supernova with iron-rich early spectra and narrow Balmer emission lines indicating interaction with a hydrogen-rich CSM. It reached ~8×10^43 erg/s peak luminosity with slow decline, revealing a progenitor mass-loss rate that surged from ~0.04 to ~0.6 M☉/yr over the final decades, producing a ~3 M☉ CSM shell. The properties suggest a white dwarf with an intermediate-mass companion undergoing increasing pre-explosion mass loss.
AI.motivation: To characterize the superluminous Type Ia supernova SN 2022erq and understand its unusual properties, particularly the evidence for strong ejecta-CSM interaction and the progenitor's pre-explosion mass-loss history.
AI.method: Photometric and spectroscopic analysis of SN 2022erq, including H-alpha diagnostics and bolometric light-curve modeling to reconstruct the progenitor's mass-loss history.
AI.result: SN 2022erq reached a peak bolometric luminosity of ~8×10^43 erg/s with slow post-peak decline. The progenitor's mass-loss rate increased from ~0.04 to ~0.6 M☉/yr over the final decades, producing a ~3 M☉ CSM shell extending to ~3.5×10^16 cm.
AI.conclusion: The progenitor system likely consists of a white dwarf and an intermediate-mass companion (~100 Myr environment) that underwent increasing mass loss prior to explosion, classifying SN 2022erq as a member of the rare Ia-CSM class.

title: Extreme particle acceleration in X-ray binaries is linked to their jets
comment: submitted to A&A
summary: The detection of multi-TeV radiation from a handful of black-hole X-ray binaries (BHXRBs) has positioned the source class as promising candidate to explain the cosmic-ray flux in the PeV energy range. To determine what distinguishes the systems detected in the gamma-ray range from the rest of the population, we build on existing catalogues of BHXRBs by including information on the radio and gamma-ray emission from these systems. We then compare the $>100$ TeV gamma-ray luminosity to different properties of the systems and evaluate the strength of the (rank) correlation between them. Additionally, we compare the distribution of BHXRBs with the positions of unassociated gamma-ray sources in the 1LHAASO and 1HGPS catalogues. We find no correlation with the mass of the compact object, the companion mass or the inclination angle. Instead, we find evidence for a strong correlation between the gamma-ray luminosity and the radio and hard-state X-ray luminosities in our sample. The limited number of gamma-ray detections means that this correlation cannot yet be claimed as statistically significant. We find indications that a high (>20\%) duty cycle (defined as fraction of time spent in outburst) might be a requirement for $>100$ TeV gamma-ray loudness. We find significant evidence ($>3σ$) that BHXRBs are located near unassociated gamma-ray sources in the region of the sky not covered by LHAASO. This evidence is only significant when comparing to BHXRBs detected in the radio band. We conclude that radio-bright BHXRBs with a high duty cycle are more likely to be detected as gamma-ray sources than sources which are not detected in the radio band or those with low duty cycles. This result indicates that the particles responsible for the gamma-ray emission are associated with the jets, either accelerated within them or via their interaction with their surroundings.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes black-hole X-ray binaries (BHXRBs) detected at >100 TeV gamma rays, finding that gamma-ray luminosity correlates with radio and hard-state X-ray luminosities, and that BHXRBs with high duty cycles (>20%) and radio-brightness are more likely to be gamma-ray sources, though limited detections prevent statistical significance. Evidence suggests particles responsible for gamma-ray emission are associated with jets.
AI.motivation: To determine what distinguishes BHXRBs detected in the gamma-ray range (>100 TeV) from the rest of the population, and to evaluate whether BHXRBs can explain the cosmic-ray flux in the PeV energy range.
AI.method: Built on existing BHXRB catalogues with radio and gamma-ray emission data; compared >100 TeV gamma-ray luminosity to system properties using rank correlation; compared BHXRB positions with unassociated gamma-ray sources in 1LHAASO and 1HGPS catalogues.
AI.result: No correlation found with compact object mass, companion mass, or inclination angle. Strong correlation found between gamma-ray luminosity and radio/hard-state X-ray luminosities (not yet statistically significant). High duty cycle (>20%) may be required for >100 TeV gamma-ray loudness. Significant evidence (>3σ) that BHXRBs are near unassociated gamma-ray sources in sky regions not covered by LHAASO, only significant for radio-detected BHXRBs.
AI.conclusion: Radio-bright BHXRBs with high duty cycles are more likely to be detected as gamma-ray sources. The gamma-ray emission is likely associated with jets, with particles accelerated within jets or via jet-environment interactions.

title: Finite-Field QED Corrections to Vacuum Birefringence and Magnetar Polarization Transport
comment: e.g. 25 pages, 5 figures
summary: {We study low-energy photon propagation in a constant magnetic field within the one-loop Heisenberg--Euler theory, retaining the refractive-index normalization $γ_s$ without expansion. Here ``finite-field'' denotes exact dependence on $B/B_{\rm cr}$ within the one-loop, constant-field approximation. The resulting birefringence is propagated into magnetar polarization transport. In a centered-dipole model, the polarization-limiting radius is unchanged to better than $10^{-12}$ because mode decoupling occurs at $\sim10^2R_{\rm NS}$, where $B\ll B_{\rm cr}$. Near the surface, however, the weak-field Cotton--Mouton expression overestimates the accumulated birefringent phase by up to a factor $2.9$ at $10^{15}$~G. At the plasma--vacuum resonance, finite-field corrections reduce the resonance density by $32\%$ and raise the adiabatic conversion energy by $14\%$ for 1E~1547.0$-$5408; the corresponding changes are factors $2.6$ and $1.37$ for 1RXS~J1708$-$4009, and factors $9.7$ and $2.13$ for SGR~1806$-$20, the latter controlled by the strong-field asymptote. The resummed one-loop parallel-mode magnetic response remains positive and develops a broad maximum near $17B_{\rm cr}$. The strictly truncated $\mathcal O(α)$ response is monotonic; therefore the maximum is a structural prediction of the resummed one-loop constitutive model, while its detailed profile and precise location require higher-loop validation. These results identify vacuum-resonance observables as the most sensitive channel for testing finite-field QED in magnetars.

AI.tldr: The paper studies photon propagation in strong magnetic fields using finite-field (exact B/B_cr) one-loop Heisenberg-Euler theory, finding that weak-field Cotton-Mouton formulas overestimate birefringent phase near magnetar surfaces (up to 2.9× at 10^15 G), while vacuum-resonance observables show large corrections (density reduced by 32-90%, adiabatic conversion energy raised by 14-113%) depending on the magnetar. The resummed one-loop parallel magnetic response develops a broad maximum near 17 B_cr, absent in truncated O(α) theory.
AI.motivation: To go beyond the weak-field expansion approximation and compute exact finite-field (i.e., full B/B_cr dependence) one-loop Heisenberg-Euler corrections for photon propagation in strong magnetic fields, and to assess their impact on observable polarization transport in magnetars.
AI.method: The authors use the one-loop Heisenberg-Euler effective action retaining full B/B_cr dependence (no weak-field expansion), compute the refractive indices and birefringence, and then propagate these effects through a centered-dipole magnetar model to study polarization-limiting radius, birefringent phase accumulation, and plasma-vacuum resonance behavior.
AI.result: (1) Polarization-limiting radius unchanged to <10^{-12} as mode decoupling occurs at large radii (~10^2 R_NS) where B≪B_cr. (2) Near the surface, weak-field Cotton-Mouton expression overestimates birefringent phase by up to factor 2.9 at 10^15 G. (3) Finite-field corrections reduce resonance density by 32-90% and raise adiabatic conversion energy by 14-113% across different magnetars. (4) Resummed one-loop parallel-mode magnetic response is positive and develops a broad maximum near 17 B_cr, unlike the monotonic truncated O(α) response.
AI.conclusion: Vacuum-resonance observables are the most sensitive channel for testing finite-field QED in magnetars; the broad maximum in the parallel-mode response near 17 B_cr is a structural prediction of the resummed one-loop model but requires higher-loop verification.
